 The program reads an integer n, then for each of n cubes, reads 6 integers (faces).
 It stores each cube's faces in a HashSet (so duplicates on a cube are ignored? Actually it adds each face to the set, so duplicates on same cube are removed).
 Then it checks if all faces are zero (notz flag). If all zero, prints 0.
 Otherwise, it iterates i from 1 to 1001, and for each i, checks if it can be formed using the cubes (aux function).
 The aux function checks if the number (1 to 3 digits) can be formed by selecting distinct cubes for each digit (order matters? Actually the cubes are used in order? Let's analyze).

 The aux function takes the array of cubes (each cube is a set of integers) and a number num.
 It breaks num into hundreds, tens, ones digits (with leading zeros treated as null? Actually if num < 100, hun is null; if num < 10, ten is null).
 Then it checks if we can assign each digit to a distinct cube (since there are 3 cubes? Wait: n is the number of cubes. In the main, cubes array size is n*6? Actually: `val cubes = Array(n * 6, { _ -> HashSet<Int>()})` That seems wrong: it creates an array of size n*6, but then in the loop `for (i in 0 until n) { for (j in 0 until 6) { ... cubes[i].add(cur) } }` So it only uses the first n elements of the array. The rest are empty sets. That's a bug in the Kotlin code? Actually the array size is n*6, but they only fill indices 0..n-1. The rest are empty HashSets. Then in aux, they access pos[0], pos[1], pos[2] assuming at least 3 cubes? But n could be less than 3? The problem likely assumes n=3? Let's read the problem context: This is a known problem "Cubes" from some contest? Typically it's about 3 cubes. The code uses pos[0], pos[1], pos[2] directly. So it assumes exactly 3 cubes? But n is read from input. If n != 3, the code would crash or behave incorrectly. However, the Kotlin code creates array of size n*6, but only uses first n. Then aux uses indices 0,1,2. So it expects n >= 3? Actually the problem might be: given n cubes (n=3), each with 6 faces, find the largest natural number that cannot be represented? Or the smallest positive integer that cannot be represented? The loop goes from 1 to 1001, and prints i-1 when aux returns false or i==1000. So it finds the first number that cannot be represented, up to 1000. If all up to 1000 can be represented, it prints 1000? Actually condition: `if (i == 1000 || !aux(cubes, i)) { println(i - 1); break }` So if i reaches 1000 and aux(1000) is true, then it prints 999? Wait: if i==1000, it prints i-1 = 999 and breaks. But if aux(1000) is false, it also prints 999. So it prints the largest number that can be represented? Actually it prints the first number that cannot be represented minus 1. So it prints the maximum consecutive integer starting from 1 that can be represented. But the loop goes to 1001, so if all numbers 1..1000 can be represented, then at i=1001, condition i==1000 is false, aux(1001) is called? But aux expects up to 3 digits? 1001 has 4 digits. The aux function only handles up to 3 digits (hun, ten, one). For 1001, num/100 = 10, so hun=10, ten=0? Actually (num%100)/10 = 0, one=1. But hun is 10 which is not a single digit. The aux function doesn't handle that. But the loop condition is `i == 1000 || !aux(cubes, i)`. So when i=1000, it prints 999 and breaks. So it never checks 1001. So the maximum number checked is 1000. So the problem is: given 3 cubes (n=3), each with 6 digits (0-9), find the largest integer k such that all numbers 1..k can be formed by selecting one face from each cube (each cube used at most once per number) and arranging them in order (hundreds, tens, ones). Leading zeros are not allowed? The aux function treats leading zeros as null and doesn't require a cube for them. For a 1-digit number, it checks if the digit is in any of the three cubes. For a 2-digit number, it checks if the ones digit is in one cube and the tens digit in another distinct cube. For a 3-digit number, it checks all permutations of assigning the three digits to the three cubes.

 So the problem assumes exactly 3 cubes. The input n is probably always 3. But the Kotlin code reads n and creates array of size n*6, but only uses first n. Then aux uses indices 0,1,2. So if n>3, it ignores extra cubes. If n<3, it will crash. We'll assume n=3.

<?php

function aux($pos, $num) {
    $hun = ($num / 100 > 0) ? (int)($num / 100) : null;
    $ten = (($num % 100) / 10 > 0) ? (int)(($num % 100) / 10) : null;
    $one = $num % 10;

    if ($ten === null && $hun === null) {
        return isset($pos[0][$one]) || isset($pos[1][$one]) || isset($pos[2][$one]);
    }
    if ($hun === null) {
        $cond = false;
        if (isset($pos[0][$one]) && (isset($pos[1][$ten]) || isset($pos[2][$ten]))) $cond = true;
        if (isset($pos[1][$one]) && (isset($pos[0][$ten]) || isset($pos[2][$ten]))) $cond = true;
        if (isset($pos[2][$one]) && (isset($pos[0][$ten]) || isset($pos[1][$ten]))) $cond = true;
        return $cond;
    }
    $cond = false;
    if (isset($pos[0][$one]) && isset($pos[1][$ten]) && isset($pos[2][$hun])) $cond = true;
    if (isset($pos[1][$one]) && isset($pos[0][$ten]) && isset($pos[2][$hun])) $cond = true;
    if (isset($pos[0][$one]) && isset($pos[2][$ten]) && isset($pos[1][$hun])) $cond = true;
    if (isset($pos[1][$one]) && isset($pos[2][$ten]) && isset($pos[0][$hun])) $cond = true;
    if (isset($pos[2][$one]) && isset($pos[1][$ten]) && isset($pos[0][$hun])) $cond = true;
    if (isset($pos[2][$one]) && isset($pos[0][$ten]) && isset($pos[1][$hun])) $cond = true;
    return $cond;
}

$input = file_get_contents('php://stdin');
$tokens = preg_split('/\s+/', trim($input));
$n = (int)$tokens[0];
$cubes = array();
$idx = 1;

source_data.prob_desc_description: Absent-minded Masha got set of n cubes for her birthday.At each of 6 faces of each cube, there is exactly one digit from 0 to 9. Masha became interested what is the largest natural x such she can make using her new cubes all integers from 1 to x.To make a number Masha can rotate her cubes and put them in a row. After that, she looks at upper faces of cubes from left to right and reads the number.The number can't contain leading zeros. It's not required to use all cubes to build a number.Pay attention: Masha can't make digit 6 from digit 9 and vice-versa using cube rotations.
source_data.prob_desc_output_spec: Print single integer — maximum number x such Masha can make any integers from 1 to x using her cubes or 0 if Masha can't make even 1.
source_data.prob_desc_input_spec: In first line integer n is given (1 ≤ n ≤ 3) — the number of cubes, Masha got for her birthday. Each of next n lines contains 6 integers aij (0 ≤ aij ≤ 9) — number on j-th face of i-th cube.
source_data.prob_desc_notes: NoteIn the first test case, Masha can build all numbers from 1 to 87, but she can't make 88 because there are no two cubes with digit 8.
